2026-09-09T03:25:38.4880753Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4881183Z 
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4881540Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4882627Z 
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4883127Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4883688Z 
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4885384Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4887261Z >
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4890246Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4893107Z >
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4894006Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4894834Z 
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4895041Z ### How to Use
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4895315Z 
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4896113Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4896907Z 
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4897106Z ```bash
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4897752Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4898577Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4899270Z ```
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4899503Z 
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4899807Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4900419Z ```bash
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4901030Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4902256Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4903220Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4904038Z ```
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4904273Z 
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4904978Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4905925Z ```bash
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4906583Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4907344Z ```
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4907585Z 
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4908099Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4908775Z ```bash
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4909400Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4910377Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4911172Z ```
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4911421Z 
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4911734Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4912456Z 
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4914023Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4915801Z 
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4916007Z ```bash
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4916532Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4917499Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4918437Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4918801Z 
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4919353Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4920505Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4921448Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4922196Z ```
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4922452Z 
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4923292Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4924294Z 
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4924492Z ```bash
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4925267Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4926264Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4927068Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4927561Z 
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4928019Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4928917Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4929538Z ```
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4929779Z 
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4930024Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4930927Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4932195Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4933297Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4934416Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4935624Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4936231Z 
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4936436Z ### Notes
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4936691Z 
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4937386Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4938956Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4940342Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4941740Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4943279Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4944524Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4945613Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4946423Z </mcp-clis>
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4946888Z <github-context>
2026-09-09T03:25:38.4947577Z The following GitHub context information is available for this workflow:
